title: The Great AI Gamble
summary: As the two world leaders in AI development and adoption, the United States and China are each operating under assumptions that justify ever-faster progress, regardless of the risks. The current thinking is not unlike the rationale once given for Stalinist brutality in the name of rapid modernization.

title: The Un-Ordered UN Order
summary: As European leaders hobnob with their counterparts at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, they must think carefully about how to navigate a fast-changing multilateral landscape. The old world belonged to rule-makers and institution-builders, but the current one favors those who can improvise.

title: AI Needs Trusted Journalism
summary: As people increasingly rely on AI chatbots for news, the already tenuous bargain between publishers and tech firms—the former invested in journalism that the latter helped audiences discover—is no longer workable. UNESCO’s proposed Guidance on Fair Compensation for News could help create a new value-exchange model.

title: How to Stop the AI-pocalypse
summary: AI could very well end democracy, if not humanity, yet efforts to slow its development may fail as companies and countries race to stay ahead. Preventing such a future will require international coordination and taxing the extreme wealth that could put unprecedented power in the hands of a tiny elite.

title: What Killed Liberalism?
summary: There is no shortage of people and ideas to blame for liberalism’s decline, but searching for a single culprit is probably futile. Two new books by Gordon Brown and Daron Acemoglu take up the harder question of how to rebuild the institutions that once gave people a sense of community and power over their lives.
